requirement:
The harness MUST expose a `references` tool with this interface:

```text
references({ selection: String?, roles: Array<"impl" | "cite" | "test">? }) -> ReferenceIndex

ReferenceIndex {
    definitions: Array<DefinitionName>,
    sites: Array<ReferenceSite>,
}

DefinitionName { name: String, kind: "requirement" | "example" }

ReferenceSite {
    name: String,
    role: "impl" | "cite" | "test",
    file: String,
    item: String?,
}
```

`selection` MUST be a {term}`requirements.references.definition_selection`.
Without `selection`, the tool MUST return
the full name and kind of every requirement and named example in full-name
order, with empty `sites`. With `selection`, it MUST return the selected definitions
in full-name order and one flattened `sites` array containing every valid
reference to any match whose role is in `roles`, defaulting to
`["impl", "cite", "test"]`, under
{cite}`requirements.references.discovery`, each naming the definition it
references, ordered by name, file, and position in the file, without line
numbers. Roles MUST be treated as a set: repeating a permitted role MUST NOT
duplicate sites or change the result.
An anchor under {cite}`requirements.references.anchors` whose role is selected
by `roles` MUST be
reported as a site for its anchored file, with the anchored node's selector as
`item` when it names one and no `item` when it names the whole file. Every
other site MUST give as `item` the selector of its smallest enclosing outline
node under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`. Only sources reference discovery considers under
{cite}`requirements.references.discovery` MUST contribute sites. If reading such a
source fails, the tool MUST return an explanatory tool error naming the source.
An invalid selection or one matching no definition MUST return an explanatory tool
error.

An empty `roles` array MUST return no sites while preserving the selected
definitions' names and kinds. An unknown role or a value other than an array of
permitted role strings MUST return an explanatory tool error. Without `selection`,
`roles` MUST NOT change the definition-name listing.

Results MUST contain no requirement text, example text, reference commentary,
or source text. Like directory listings, they MUST
NOT become evidence inputs; the model requests the sources it relies on with the
`habeas` tool. For example,
`references({selection: "requirements.cli.status", roles: ["impl"]})` MUST
locate only that subject's implementation references and anchors, without
supplying their source or recording evidence inputs.
rationale:
The reviewed tests cover each obligation of `requirements.authoring.reference_index`, and the assertions would catch plausible violations. I did not request any implementation source.

**Interface**
- `references_tool_is_advertised_with_an_optional_selection` in `src/authoring/tools.rs` asserts the exact parameter schema. `selection` is an optional string, and `roles` is an array of `impl`, `cite` or `test` that defaults to all three. It also checks the description.

**Listing without `selection`**
- `references_list_names_and_flattened_sites_without_recording_inputs` writes the definitions in the order `ready`, `other`, `case`. It asserts the result is exactly `case`, `other`, `ready` with the right kinds and `sites: []`. That checks full-name ordering rather than definition order.
- A `definition` term (`requirements.word`) is not listed.
- The same test shows `roles: ["impl"]` without a selection leaves the listing unchanged.

**With `selection`**
- *Exact name:* a name without `*` selects exactly that definition.
- *Glob:* a glob returns the same ordered definitions.
- *Flattened sites:* the result is one flattened `sites` array.
- *Site ordering:* sites are ordered by name, then file, then position.
  - The first site is `requirements.other`, so names are sorted.
  - The fenced-file case puts `src/fenced.rs` before `src/lib.rs`. Sorting by role would have put the `cite` first, so this shows files are sorted.
  - Within `src/lib.rs`, `fn[zeta]` comes before `fn[work]`. That is source position, not alphabetical order.
- *Item selectors:* a comment inside a function body gets `fn[work]`. Markdown sites get a `section@…` item or null. File anchors have a null item, and node anchors have a selector such as `section[Skill]` (in `references_report_anchors_as_file_or_node_sites`).
- *No line numbers:* the exact JSON equality assertions rule out extra fields.
- *Fenced references:* a fenced `{impl}` is reported as a site. A `{fixme}` and an unclosed fence are not.
- *Role filtering:* `roles: ["impl"]` returns only the impl site and anchor in both tests. `["impl","impl"]` returns the same result without duplicates. `roles: []` returns the definitions with no sites.
- *Invalid roles:* `null`, `"impl"`, `["fixme"]` and `[1]` each return an error mentioning "role".
- *Invalid selections:* a missing name, a vocabulary term, an invalid name, an empty string, a non-string selection and an unknown parameter each return an error.

**Considered sources**
- `references_report_only_sites_in_considered_sources` checks that an untracked file and a path disallowed by the evidence configuration contribute no sites. Only `src/tracked.rs` is reported.
- `references_name_a_considered_source_that_cannot_be_read` checks that an unreadable considered source gives an error naming `src/locked.rs`.
- The detailed discovery and anchor-validation rules belong to `requirements.references.discovery` and `requirements.references.anchors`, which this subject only cites.

**No text and no evidence inputs**
- Every `dispatch` assertion in the tools tests checks that `inputs` is empty.
- The CLI test `implementation_discovery_has_no_text_or_evidence_until_the_model_requests_a_read` in `tests/authoring_cli.rs` checks that the tool result contains no requirement text, no gap text and no source text. It also checks that the `references` call does not appear in the recorded evidence inputs. Only the later `habeas` read does.
- The `references` call with `roles: ["impl"]` matches the example in the requirement.
- The paging test `reference_results_page_definitions_then_sites` checks that pages hold no inputs and that sites follow all definitions.

I found no gap: each clause has a test that exercises it and asserts its outcome.

The harness MUST expose a `references` tool with this interface:
```text
references({ selection: String?, roles: Array<"impl" | "cite" | "test">? }) -> ReferenceIndex
ReferenceIndex {
definitions: Array<DefinitionName>,
sites: Array<ReferenceSite>,
DefinitionName { name: String, kind: "requirement" | "example" }
ReferenceSite {
name: String,
role: "impl" | "cite" | "test",
file: String,
item: String?,
`selection` MUST be a {term}`requirements.references.definition_selection`.
Without `selection`, the tool MUST return
the full name and kind of every requirement and named example in full-name
order, with empty `sites`. With `selection`, it MUST return the selected definitions
in full-name order and one flattened `sites` array containing every valid
reference to any match whose role is in `roles`, defaulting to
`["impl", "cite", "test"]`, under
{cite}`requirements.references.discovery`, each naming the definition it
references, ordered by name, file, and position in the file, without line
numbers. Roles MUST be treated as a set: repeating a permitted role MUST NOT
duplicate sites or change the result.
An anchor under {cite}`requirements.references.anchors` whose role is selected
by `roles` MUST be
reported as a site for its anchored file, with the anchored node's selector as
`item` when it names one and no `item` when it names the whole file. Every
other site MUST give as `item` the selector of its smallest enclosing outline
node under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`. Only sources reference discovery considers under
{cite}`requirements.references.discovery` MUST contribute sites. If reading such a
source fails, the tool MUST return an explanatory tool error naming the source.
An invalid selection or one matching no definition MUST return an explanatory tool
error.
An empty `roles` array MUST return no sites while preserving the selected
definitions' names and kinds. An unknown role or a value other than an array of
permitted role strings MUST return an explanatory tool error. Without `selection`,
`roles` MUST NOT change the definition-name listing.
Results MUST contain no requirement text, example text, reference commentary,
or source text. Like directory listings, they MUST
NOT become evidence inputs; the model requests the sources it relies on with the
`habeas` tool. For example,
`references({selection: "requirements.cli.status", roles: ["impl"]})` MUST
locate only that subject's implementation references and anchors, without
supplying their source or recording evidence inputs.
:::{req} discovery
Habeas MUST find the references of {cite}`requirements.references.roles`
in project source files, where {cite}`requirements.references.reference_contexts`
says they count, and MUST fail with the source file and line if a
name has no matching `{req}` or `{example}` definition. In Markdown, escaped
roles and roles in code examples MUST remain literal. Reference discovery MUST
consider the following files: in a Git worktree, files present in
the Git index, including staged new files; outside Git, all project files; in
both cases excluding the project-root `book` and `evidence` directories, `.git`
and `target` directories at any depth, and paths disallowed by
{cite}`requirements.configuration.evidence_paths`. Evidence snapshots and
generated build output MUST therefore not be counted as source references.
:::{req} anchors
A `{req}` declaration MAY list `:impl:` and `:test:` options, and an `{example}`
declaration MAY list `:test:` options, immediately after its opening fence and
before its body, one per option line, naming a project file path or
`path#selector` for one outline node under
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`. Each anchor MUST be an `{impl}` or `{test}` edge, under
{cite}`requirements.references.roles`, from the definition to the anchored file or
node, for files that cannot or should not carry a reference themselves.
Paths MUST follow the path rules in {cite}`requirements.ci.schema`. Option lines
MUST NOT form part of the definition's text for evidence comparison or for
requirements inputs, and MUST NOT render as body text.
For each `:test:` anchor, the harness MUST include the selected file or node's
source text in the initial model request under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs` and MUST record that selection
as an evidence input under {cite}`requirements.references.evidence_coverage`,
so changing that source makes the evidence stale.
A `:impl:` anchor alone MUST NOT require an input selecting its source. A path or selector that
does not resolve to a readable, permitted file or node MUST be a validation error naming the
definition and the path; authoring MUST report it before inference. Any other option line in a `{req}` or
`{example}` declaration MUST be a validation error.
:::{req} outline_comments
Each documented profile defines which grammar nodes are comments; the Markdown
profile's comments are HTML comment blocks, so an inline HTML comment within a
paragraph remains ordinary paragraph text. In every supported language, comments on consecutive lines with no other source
between them MUST form one comment run. A comment that follows other source on
the same line, including another comment, MUST form a run by itself and MUST belong to the innermost outline node
containing that line. Any other run MUST belong to the next outline node that
starts after it within the smallest node containing it; when that container has
no such node, the run MUST belong to the container, which is the root node at top
level. A profile MAY bind a comment kind to its container
instead: such a run MUST belong to the smallest node containing it. The Rust
profile MUST bind inner doc comments (`//!`, `/*!`) to their container, so a
file-level inner doc comment belongs to the root node. Habeas MUST retain the
one-based line and UTF-8 byte column of each inline role’s opening brace or
fenced reference’s first opening colon. When siblings share a line, the
reference belongs to the item owning the comment at that position. A reference
in a comment MUST count for the node its run belongs to under
{cite}`requirements.references.coverage.tests` and
{cite}`requirements.references.authoring_inputs`.
:::{definition} definition_selection
:phrase: definition selection
A full requirement or example name, or a definition glob, identifying the
requirements and named examples it matches under
{cite}`requirements.references.definition_globs`. A name without `*` selects
exactly that definition.
